guides.wedding-vow-writer.title: Wedding Vows: How to Write Your Own (With Examples)
guides.wedding-vow-writer.desc: A practical structure for personal wedding vows: what to promise, what to leave out, how long they should be, and short examples to adapt.
guides.wedding-vow-writer.lead: Good vows are specific and short. The memorable ones name one real habit, one promise for hard days, and one hope — not a list of superlatives.
guides.wedding-vow-writer.f1v: Two to three minutes, roughly 200–300 words per person
guides.wedding-vow-writer.f2v: A memory, three promises, one line about the future
guides.wedding-vow-writer.f3v: Write as you speak; read it aloud before finishing
guides.wedding-vow-writer.f4v: Print a card; do not rely on a phone screen
guides.wedding-vow-writer.s1: Draft in three passes. First write everything without editing. Then cut anything that would embarrass a grandparent or that only the two of you understand. Last, read it aloud and remove sentences you run out of breath on. Promises should be verifiable — 'I will make coffee on Sundays' lands harder than 'I will always make you happy'.
guides.wedding-vow-writer.s2: In the US personal vows are common alongside or instead of traditional ones; in the UK many couples use the legal wording and add a short personal reading. Catholic and Jewish ceremonies often require set texts, so check with the officiant before writing. If you marry abroad, the legal declaration may need to be in the local language, with personal vows kept separate and translated for guests.
guides.wedding-vow-writer.s3: The most common mistake is writing a speech instead of a vow — a vow is a promise, not a tribute. Avoid inside jokes, ex-partner references, and anything that needs context. Also agree on length and tone with your partner in advance so one person does not deliver three minutes while the other says two sentences.
guides.wedding-vow-writer.q1: How long should wedding vows be?
guides.wedding-vow-writer.a1: About two to three minutes each, or 200–300 words. Agree a shared length so the exchange feels balanced.
guides.wedding-vow-writer.q2: Can we write our own vows in a religious ceremony?
guides.wedding-vow-writer.a2: Often yes as an addition, but the required legal or sacramental wording cannot be replaced. Ask the officiant early.
guides.wedding-vow-writer.a3: Keep the content private if you like, but agree on length, tone and whether they are memorised. Surprises should not create a mismatch.
